content: The document titled Target Product Profiles for Tuberculosis Diagnosis and Detection of Drug Resistance was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2024. It is available in both electronic and print versions, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-009769-8 and 978-92-4-009770-4. The publication is protected under a Creative Commons license, which allows users to copy, redistribute, and adapt the content for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and any adaptations must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. If a translation is created, it must include a disclaimer stating that the translation was not produced by WHO and that the original English version remains the authoritative edition. The document emphasizes that WHO does not endorse any specific organizations, products, or services mentioned within it. Any proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters, and the responsibility for interpreting and using the material lies with the reader. WHO disclaims liability for any damages arising from the use of the content. The publication was developed by WHO’s Global Tuberculosis Programme with contributions from experts in public health policy, tuberculosis program management, and the diagnosis and care of tuberculosis patients. The development process was led by Nazir Ismail, with support from Alexei Korobitsyn and Lice González-Angulo, under the guidance of Matteo Zignol and the overall direction of Tereza Kasaeva, Director of WHO’s Global Tuberculosis Programme. The document includes updated components related to target product profiles (TPPs) for rapid diagnostic tests to detect pulmonary tuberculosis at peripheral levels. WHO acknowledges the contributions of the Scientific TPP Development Group, which includes experts from various countries and institutions. These experts provided input on the development and refinement of the TPPs, ensuring their relevance and applicability in diverse settings. Additionally, WHO recognizes the contributions of technical, development, and regulatory agencies, as well as members of the New Diagnostics Working Group of the Stop TB Partnership. The document also acknowledges the input of individuals who participated in online public calls for comments and Delphi-like consultation processes, which supported the development of the TPPs. The publication includes acknowledgments for modeling work and feedback provided by various experts and organizations. It also highlights the contributions of WHO Secretariat members and regional office representatives who supported the development and finalization of the TPPs. The document reflects a collaborative effort involving a wide range of stakeholders to advance tuberculosis diagnosis and drug resistance detection.
